PR #459 changed the parent-chain inspection to lstat(), explicitly rejects S_ISLNK with ANCHOR_PARENT_SYMLINK_FORBIDDEN, and preserves root-owner plus group/other-write checks.
PR #459 had already passed its exact-head self-hosted regression run 31534490002 before promotion.
PR #459 was merged into current main as c20a9277b95df4ad6cbcba11ed53a4f07e1745f1.

r1_hypothesis.hypothesis: Replacing stat() with lstat() and denying symlink parent components closes the observed parent-symlink transplant path without weakening the existing ownership/writeability boundary.
r1_hypothesis.mechanism: The guard now reasons about the directory entry itself rather than the followed target for every anchor parent component; symlink presence becomes directly observable and fail-closed.
r1_hypothesis.predicted_if_right: Direct root-owned non-writable parent chains remain admitted by this sub-check, symlink parent chains are denied, writable parents remain denied.
r1_hypothesis.predicted_if_wrong: The focused regression or current-main composition/static integrity would fail, or a parent symlink would remain indistinguishable from a directory.

r3_counter_reality.strongest_counterhypothesis: A hidden filesystem permission mechanism could still make a root-owned mode-safe parent writable by an unprivileged Frank user while evading the V5 mode-bit check.
r3_counter_reality.discriminator: POSIX ACL named-user write permission counterworld

unusual_experiment.purpose: Test whether a root-owned directory could retain apparently safe mode bits while a named-user POSIX ACL grants write permission, bypassing the V5 group/other-write check.
unusual_experiment.method: On a disposable local Linux directory, encode a system.posix_acl_access xattr granting UID 65534 rwx while the directory is root-owned; observe resulting mode and verify the named user can create a file.
unusual_experiment.interpretation: Linux reflects the POSIX ACL mask write permission in the group-class mode bits, so the existing V5 group-write rejection catches this named-user write ACL case. No ACL-specific patch is justified by this experiment.
